tools.name: gridforge_qualify
tools.description: Free. Up to seven numbers about an existing air-cooled hall in (at least three; each one you leave out is an assumption named in the answer), one answer out: which physical constraint binds first when you try to deploy AI racks in it, how many racks fit as found, and which item sets the time to power (labelled 'assumed lead time, not a date' when that item's lead time is an assumption). Use this to triage a portfolio before paying for anything.
tools.returns: binding constraint, racks as found and after relief (each with racks_evidence, the evidence class of that rack count as a short code such as E0: the weakest class among the constraints that cap it), the item that sets the date (null, with sets_the_date_reason, when no date can be given: nothing is deployable, or a lead time on the path is missing because transformers or UPS were not declared), and the inputs nobody has measured (when you send assumed_fields, also inputs_declared_assumed, which lists only what you declared; when you send contracted_MW and no firm_capacity_MVA, inputs_derived_assumed, the firm capacity the qualifier derived, as an assumption). No capital cost or dated lead times in this free read: the metered /v1/compare (it needs an API key) returns indicative capital and weeks with evidence classes, and the paid documents add the full costed ladder.
tools.evidence_boundary: Directional only: a figure you send is treated as yours (E5) unless you name it in assumed_fields (E0), what you leave out is assumed and disclosed in intake.gaps, and this free answer carries no capital cost and no dated lead time.

inputSchema.description: Seven figures about one air-cooled hall, and some options. Send at least three of these seven figures; each one you omit is an assumption named in the answer (library default, listed under intake.gaps and, with the way you left it out, under figures_not_supplied). Fewer than three is refused with 422, and no one figure is required: any three are enough. A figure sent as null is not sent: it counts as omitted, and the answer says so. Each figure you do send is checked by its own name against the same plausibility bounds the engine's intake uses (a refusal names the figure you sent, with the limit). The engine does not validate a request against this schema before running it: a key that is not listed here is not read as a figure and is ignored, except cost_evidence, which this route does not take and refuses with 422.

positions_available.description: Rack positions that can be released.

firm_capacity_MVA.description: Optional. Firm capacity of the grid connection, MVA, sent as a plain number. It is a real input: a value below the connection the engine would otherwise derive lowers the firm-supply headroom. Omit it (and send contracted_MW) and the engine derives one from contracted_MW, lists it as an assumption (E0) under inputs_derived_assumed in the result, and adds a required grid.firm_capacity_MVA row to intake.gaps. That list is separate from inputs_declared_assumed, which holds only what you declared. firm_capacity_MVA cannot be named in assumed_fields.

platform.description: Optional. The rack platform the hall is tested against (GET /v1/platforms lists them). It sets the per-rack electrical and thermal load, so it changes the result. An id the library does not carry is refused with 422.

assumed_fields.description: Optional. Declares which of the figures above you are sending as ASSUMPTIONS rather than as this hall's own data, for example values copied from a reference template. Each entry must be one of the seven figures (contracted_MW, current_site_peak_MW, current_it_load_MW, busway_ampacity_A, tapoff_max_A, plant_supply_C, positions_available), named at most once, and the same request must also send that figure (a figure you did not send cannot be declared assumed). Effect: a named figure is classed E0 (assumption) instead of E5 (supplied by the client) in the result's basis and evidence, and is listed in the result's inputs_declared_assumed (path, input, unit, value, evidence "E0", note); intake.assumed_count says how many, while intake.completeness and required_inputs_missing still count a declared figure as supplied. It changes the label and not the arithmetic: the racks and the binding constraint are the same with or without it, and nothing you send can raise a class above E0. Omitted, null or an empty list, the request is answered as if the field did not exist. A name that is not one of the seven, a repeat, a value that is not a list, or a figure you did not send is refused with 422, naming the entry and listing the allowed names. An engine that serves this field reports capabilities.qualify_assumed_fields: true at GET /v1/version.

client.description: Optional. Your organisation's name. A label for your own records: the qualifier writes it into the intake it builds and it changes no figure in the result.

reference.description: Optional. Your own reference for this hall or request. A label for your own records: the qualifier writes it into the intake it builds and it changes no figure in the result.

site_name.description: Optional. The site's name. A label for your own records: the qualifier writes it into the intake it builds and it changes no figure in the result.

metro.description: Optional. The metro area. A label for your own records: the qualifier writes it into the intake it builds and it changes no figure in the result.

country.description: Optional. The country. A label for your own records: the qualifier writes it into the intake it builds and it changes no figure in the result.

hall_id.description: Optional. The hall's identifier. A label for your own records: the qualifier writes it into the intake it builds and it changes no figure in the result.

tools.name: gridforge_estimate
tools.description: Free, no API key, never metered. What would a call cost? Name an endpoint (and, for the portfolio, how many halls) and get the units, the unit price and the cost in euro cents BEFORE spending anything. With an API key it also says whether the call fits what is left of the key's allowance or cap. Use it before any paid tool, especially in a loop.
tools.returns: endpoint, units, unit_price_cents, estimated_cents, billable, free, the rule that produced the units, and (with a key) the remaining allowance and whether the call fits.
tools.evidence_boundary: Arithmetic on the published rate card, not an engineering result: it prices a call and says whether it fits an allowance, and it runs no model.

endpoint.description: The engine route to price, e.g. /v1/study.

hall_count.description: Halls in a /v1/portfolio request (one unit each). A portfolio request ranks at most 50 halls: a larger hall_count is refused with 422, as the request would be.

body.description: Optional: the request body you intend to send; the units are read from it exactly as the meter would.

tools.name: gridforge_screen
tools.description: Density Screen. A full intake in, a screening read out: every constraint evaluated, and the headroom ladder: each relief in binding order, with its cost, lead time and the racks it unlocks.
tools.returns: screen payload (with grid_queue_context: the measured US queue statistic beside the assumed grid wait), or the rendered screening document.
tools.evidence_boundary: Screening mode: the constraints are solved from the intake you send, anything you leave out is filled from library defaults and disclosed as an assumption, and each figure carries its evidence class (E0 to E7).

intake.description: A GridForge intake document. GET /v1/intake/template for the blank form with every field, or supply a sparse one — anything absent is filled from library defaults and reported as an assumption. Optional hall.occupied_positions (a non-negative whole number, or {value, evidence, note, source}; E5 when you supply it, never higher) is the number of rack positions already occupied. Omitted, the engine does not know it: it is listed as an optional gap, and the busway check against the load already in the hall reads every position that is not free as occupied and says so as an assumption (E0). Declare 0 to confirm that nothing is occupied. It changes no rack count, cost or date.

grid_queue_region.description: Optional. Which of LBNL's US regions the measured queue statistic in grid_queue_context is drawn from; omit for the pooled US figure. Context only: it changes no number and no date.

electricity_price_state.description: Optional. Which US state's published average electricity price retail_price_context is drawn from; omit for the US average. Context only: it changes no price and no cost.

tools.name: gridforge_compare
tools.description: Time-to-Power scenario comparison. A full intake in; the scenarios it defines out, side by side: racks as found and after relief, the constraint that binds, the time to full capacity with its low/high band and evidence class (and, in date_basis / date_label, whether an assumed lead time sits behind it: 'assumed lead time, not a date'), capital and what is unpriced, and how each differs from the baseline. A scenario with an unknown lead time gets no date and a reason, never a small number; nothing is ranked on a figure it does not have. Same solve as gridforge_screen, same inputs, same numbers.
tools.returns: gridforge/ttp-compare/1: scenarios[] (each with as_found.racks and after_ladder.racks, and racks_evidence beside each: the evidence class of that rack count as a short code such as E0), ranking, grade, caveats, grid_queue_context (measured US queue statistic, context only), request_digest, provenance.
tools.evidence_boundary: Same solve as the screen: a scenario with an unknown lead time gets no date and a reason, nothing is ranked on a figure it does not have, and a date that rests on an assumed lead time is labelled 'assumed lead time, not a date'.

baseline.description: Scenario id the others are compared with. Default: the first.

tools.evidence_boundary: Every numeric requirement is derived from the capacity model, at the site's own conditions, and names the constraint it came from; it is a specification to tender against, not a supplier's quotation.

tools.returns: ranked bids with scores, schedule impact, and optional cost-library lines.
tools.evidence_boundary: Ranks only the supplier responses you send, against the capacity model; a non-compliant bid is never ranked above a compliant one, and quote lines returned with evidence_only are not accepted until a person reviews them.

ingest.description: also return the cost-library lines the winning response implies

evidence_only.description: return the validated or invalid quote lines instead of a ranking; nothing is accepted until a person reviews it

tools.name: gridforge_power_assess
tools.description: The Power Readiness Case: what is stopping this site reaching the target capacity, what fixes it, what that costs, what it does to the schedule, and what to do next. Composes the same solved scenario as gridforge_screen/gridforge_study into one decision object: current deployable racks vs. the target, the binding constraint, every priced and dated rung on the headroom ladder, the critical-path dependencies that set the earliest time to power (each marked when its lead time is only assumed), the calibration state behind every number, and one deterministic next action. Never invents a price, a lead time or a date — every figure traces to the engine or an explicit input, with its evidence class attached.
tools.returns: capacity (current/target/gap; target_reachable and gap_racks_after_ladder say whether the full headroom ladder reaches the target, and what is still missing when it does not), binding_constraint, headroom_ladder (every relief priced and dated), time_to_power (critical item and dependencies), evidence (calibration state, evidence classes used), and next_action (which leads with the fact when the target is not reachable).
tools.evidence_boundary: Composed from the same solved scenario as the screen and the study: no price, lead time or date is invented, every figure traces to the engine or an explicit input with its evidence class, and the calibration state is stated.

intake.description: A GridForge intake document. target_racks.description: the rack count the customer actually needs; omit to size the gap against what the full headroom ladder itself can reach

tools.name: gridforge_power_deploy_assess
tools.description: The BTM Power Deployment Assessment: given a real load profile and the generation/BESS units actually on the table, compares GRID ONLY, GRID + GENERATION, GRID + BESS and GRID + BESS + GENERATION under one deterministic N/N+1/N+2/2N contingency test each, with CAPEX and lead time read from whatever the request declared (never priced at zero when a unit is uncosted — that architecture is marked not-yet-comparable instead). Answers 'what combination of grid, generation and storage gets this load to firm power by this date, and what does each option cost.' Never invents a price, a lead time, or a PASS — a generator with no declared availability escalates a would-be PASS to REQUIRES_ENGINEERING_STUDY rather than assuming perfect reliability.
tools.returns: load_profile summary (peak/mean/load-factor/ramp/step-events, with its own evidence class), capacity (grid-only vs. target, the gap), architectures (each with contingency status, CAPEX, lead time, whether fully costed, readiness_gates — interconnection/protection/fuel/permitting/electrical/reliability, each PASS/FAIL/MISSING_DATA/REQUIRES_ENGINEERING_STUDY/REQUIRES_LICENSED_REVIEW/NOT_APPLICABLE with its reason and what's missing — plus rfq_ready [enough data to prepare an RFQ], external_clearances_required [who still has to sign off — protection, utility, permitting], and execution_ready [cleared to build, which on-site generation/storage architectures will almost never show as true from screening alone]), and next_action, which names a missing readiness field before it ever says 'proceed to RFQ', always separates RFQ-readiness from build clearance, and states which objective was used, why, and the trade-off against the runner-up architecture — never a silent 'cheapest wins'.
tools.evidence_boundary: Compares architectures only on the load profile and units you declare: a unit with no declared cost leaves its architecture not-yet-comparable rather than priced at zero, and a generator with no declared availability can never yield a plain PASS (it is escalated to REQUIRES_ENGINEERING_STUDY).

load_profile.description: either {csv: 'timestamp,kW\n...'} from a real interval export, or {flat_kW: n} for a screening-level single-figure assumption (explicitly weaker evidence).

grid_firm_MW.description: firm import available from the grid connection today

ride_through_hours.description: the outage duration a battery must be sized against; defaults to 2h if omitted

objective.description: What the architecture ranking optimises for: max_compute (most firm capacity), min_cost (lowest CAPEX among architectures that pass their own contingency test), or fastest (shortest critical-path lead time). The winner is never chosen by lowest cost silently — next_action always states which objective was used and the trade-off against the runner-up.

operating_mode.description: how you run this unit. 'continuous': it is already running, so its start-up is never on the critical path. 'standby': it is offline until needed, so declared storage must carry the load it is relied on for until it is up, or the result is flagged for engineering study. Omit it and nothing about start-up is assumed or checked (the result says so).

startup_time_min.description: start-up time from offline to carrying load, minutes; replaces the library default for the technology

fuel_type.description: e.g. 'natural gas' — feeds the fuel readiness gate; omitting it leaves that gate MISSING_DATA

grid_forming.description: feeds the electrical readiness gate — more than one grid-forming source across the architecture requires a controls arbitration study

interconnection.description: utility, pcc_voltage_kV, import_capacity_MW — feeds the interconnection readiness gate. Omitting it leaves that gate MISSING_DATA, never a guessed PASS.

permitting.description: e.g. {emissions_status, noise_status} — feeds the permitting readiness gate.

tools.name: gridforge_power_deploy_spec
tools.description: A tender-ready technical specification for a BTM architecture's generation and storage units: every numeric requirement (nameplate rating, availability/forced-outage rate, start-up time, ramp rate, fuel, BESS power/energy/SOC window) derived from the declared unit and traceable to it, plus a weighted evaluation matrix and a machine-readable response schedule. Same request shape as gridforge_power_deploy_assess — this is what 'proceed to procurement' in that tool's next_action actually produces.
tools.returns: the specification document, or its summary and response template as JSON.
tools.evidence_boundary: Every numeric requirement is derived from the generation or storage unit you declared and traceable to it; it is a tender specification, not a supplier's quotation.

architecture.description: one of the compared architecture labels, e.g. 'GRID + BESS + GENERATION'; selects the units tendered

require_rfq_ready.description: refuse unless the engine itself finds this architecture RFQ-ready

load_profile.description: unused by this tool but part of the shared request shape; pass {flat_kW: 0} if omitting a real profile

ride_through_hours.description: the outage duration a battery must be sized against; defaults to 2h if omitted

interconnection.description: utility, pcc_voltage_kV, import_capacity_MW — feeds the interconnection readiness gate. Omitting it leaves that gate MISSING_DATA, never a guessed PASS.

permitting.description: e.g. {emissions_status, noise_status} — feeds the permitting readiness gate.

tools.name: gridforge_power_deploy_bids
tools.description: Rank supplier responses to a BTM tender package (gridforge_power_deploy_spec) with the same comparison rules as gridforge_bids: mandatory non-compliance is never outranked by price, incomplete responses are disqualified not guessed at, and installation method and evidence quality are left to an engineer. Send the same deployment request and architecture the package was built from, plus the completed response schedules.
tools.returns: the ranked comparison, the leading compliant supplier (or null) and the note.
tools.evidence_boundary: Ranks only the responses you send: mandatory non-compliance is never outranked by price, incomplete responses are disqualified rather than guessed at, and installation method and evidence quality are left to an engineer.

ride_through_hours.description: the outage duration a battery must be sized against; defaults to 2h if omitted

interconnection.description: utility, pcc_voltage_kV, import_capacity_MW — feeds the interconnection readiness gate. Omitting it leaves that gate MISSING_DATA, never a guessed PASS.

permitting.description: e.g. {emissions_status, noise_status} — feeds the permitting readiness gate.

tools.evidence_boundary: Built from what the engine already found for this intake; the price it states is the named engagement's catalogue price.

tools.name: gridforge_qualify
tools.description: Free. Up to seven numbers about an existing air-cooled hall in (at least three; each one you leave out is an assumption named in the answer), one answer out: which physical constraint binds first when you try to deploy AI racks in it, how many racks fit as found, and which item sets the time to power (labelled 'assumed lead time, not a date' when that item's lead time is an assumption). Use this to triage a portfolio before paying for anything.

inputSchema.description: Seven figures about one air-cooled hall, and some options. Send at least three of these seven figures; each one you omit is an assumption named in the answer (library default, listed under intake.gaps and, with the way you left it out, under figures_not_supplied). Fewer than three is refused with 422, and no one figure is required: any three are enough. A figure sent as null is not sent: it counts as omitted, and the answer says so. Each figure you do send is checked by its own name against the same plausibility bounds the engine's intake uses (a refusal names the figure you sent, with the limit). The engine does not validate a request against this schema before running it: a key that is not listed here is not read as a figure and is ignored, except cost_evidence, which this route does not take and refuses with 422.

positions_available.description: Rack positions that can be released.

firm_capacity_MVA.description: Optional. Firm capacity of the grid connection, MVA, sent as a plain number. It is a real input: a value below the connection the engine would otherwise derive lowers the firm-supply headroom. Omit it (and send contracted_MW) and the engine derives one from contracted_MW, lists it as an assumption (E0) under inputs_derived_assumed in the result, and adds a required grid.firm_capacity_MVA row to intake.gaps. That list is separate from inputs_declared_assumed, which holds only what you declared. firm_capacity_MVA cannot be named in assumed_fields.

platform.description: Optional. The rack platform the hall is tested against (GET /v1/platforms lists them). It sets the per-rack electrical and thermal load, so it changes the result. An id the library does not carry is refused with 422.

assumed_fields.description: Optional. Declares which of the figures above you are sending as ASSUMPTIONS rather than as this hall's own data, for example values copied from a reference template. Each entry must be one of the seven figures (contracted_MW, current_site_peak_MW, current_it_load_MW, busway_ampacity_A, tapoff_max_A, plant_supply_C, positions_available), named at most once, and the same request must also send that figure (a figure you did not send cannot be declared assumed). Effect: a named figure is classed E0 (assumption) instead of E5 (supplied by the client) in the result's basis and evidence, and is listed in the result's inputs_declared_assumed (path, input, unit, value, evidence "E0", note); intake.assumed_count says how many, while intake.completeness and required_inputs_missing still count a declared figure as supplied. It changes the label and not the arithmetic: the racks and the binding constraint are the same with or without it, and nothing you send can raise a class above E0. Omitted, null or an empty list, the request is answered as if the field did not exist. A name that is not one of the seven, a repeat, a value that is not a list, or a figure you did not send is refused with 422, naming the entry and listing the allowed names. An engine that serves this field reports capabilities.qualify_assumed_fields: true at GET /v1/version.

Optional hall.occupied_positions (a non-negative whole number, or {value, evidence, note, source}; E5 when you supply it, never higher) is the number of rack positions already occupied. Omitted, the engine does not know it: it is listed as an optional gap, and the busway check against the load already in the hall reads every position that is not free as occupied and says so as an assumption (E0). Declare 0 to confirm that nothing is occupied. It changes no rack count, cost or date.

tools.name: gridforge_bids
tools.description: Compare supplier responses against the capacity model: what each bid does to the energisation date and to deployable rack count, not only what it costs. A non-compliant bid is never ranked above a compliant one.

tools.name: gridforge_power_assess
tools.description: The Power Readiness Case: what is stopping this site reaching the target capacity, what fixes it, what that costs, what it does to the schedule, and what to do next. Composes the same solved scenario as gridforge_screen/gridforge_study into one decision object: current deployable racks vs. the target, the binding constraint, every priced and dated rung on the headroom ladder, the critical-path dependencies that set the earliest time to power (each marked when its lead time is only assumed), the calibration state behind every number, and one deterministic next action. Never invents a price, a lead time or a date — every figure traces to the engine or an explicit input, with its evidence class attached.

target_racks.description: the rack count the customer actually needs; omit to size the gap against what the full headroom ladder itself can reach

tools.name: gridforge_power_deploy_assess
tools.description: The BTM Power Deployment Assessment: given a real load profile and the generation/BESS units actually on the table, compares GRID ONLY, GRID + GENERATION, GRID + BESS and GRID + BESS + GENERATION under one deterministic N/N+1/N+2/2N contingency test each, with CAPEX and lead time read from whatever the request declared (never priced at zero when a unit is uncosted — that architecture is marked not-yet-comparable instead). Answers 'what combination of grid, generation and storage gets this load to firm power by this date, and what does each option cost.' Never invents a price, a lead time, or a PASS — a generator with no declared availability escalates a would-be PASS to REQUIRES_ENGINEERING_STUDY rather than assuming perfect reliability.

load_profile.description: either {csv: 'timestamp,kW\n...'} from a real interval export, or {flat_kW: n} for a screening-level single-figure assumption (explicitly weaker evidence).

grid_firm_MW.description: firm import available from the grid connection today

ride_through_hours.description: the outage duration a battery must be sized against; defaults to 2h if omitted

objective.description: What the architecture ranking optimises for: max_compute (most firm capacity), min_cost (lowest CAPEX among architectures that pass their own contingency test), or fastest (shortest critical-path lead time). The winner is never chosen by lowest cost silently — next_action always states which objective was used and the trade-off against the runner-up.

operating_mode.description: how you run this unit. 'continuous': it is already running, so its start-up is never on the critical path. 'standby': it is offline until needed, so declared storage must carry the load it is relied on for until it is up, or the result is flagged for engineering study. Omit it and nothing about start-up is assumed or checked (the result says so).

startup_time_min.description: start-up time from offline to carrying load, minutes; replaces the library default for the technology

fuel_type.description: e.g. 'natural gas' — feeds the fuel readiness gate; omitting it leaves that gate MISSING_DATA

grid_forming.description: feeds the electrical readiness gate — more than one grid-forming source across the architecture requires a controls arbitration study

interconnection.description: utility, pcc_voltage_kV, import_capacity_MW — feeds the interconnection readiness gate. Omitting it leaves that gate MISSING_DATA, never a guessed PASS.

permitting.description: e.g. {emissions_status, noise_status} — feeds the permitting readiness gate.

tools.name: gridforge_power_deploy_spec
tools.description: A tender-ready technical specification for a BTM architecture's generation and storage units: every numeric requirement (nameplate rating, availability/forced-outage rate, start-up time, ramp rate, fuel, BESS power/energy/SOC window) derived from the declared unit and traceable to it, plus a weighted evaluation matrix and a machine-readable response schedule. Same request shape as gridforge_power_deploy_assess — this is what 'proceed to procurement' in that tool's next_action actually produces.

architecture.description: one of the compared architecture labels, e.g. 'GRID + BESS + GENERATION'; selects the units tendered

require_rfq_ready.description: refuse unless the engine itself finds this architecture RFQ-ready

load_profile.description: unused by this tool but part of the shared request shape; pass {flat_kW: 0} if omitting a real profile

ride_through_hours.description: the outage duration a battery must be sized against; defaults to 2h if omitted

interconnection.description: utility, pcc_voltage_kV, import_capacity_MW — feeds the interconnection readiness gate. Omitting it leaves that gate MISSING_DATA, never a guessed PASS.

permitting.description: e.g. {emissions_status, noise_status} — feeds the permitting readiness gate.

tools.name: gridforge_power_deploy_bids
tools.description: Rank supplier responses to a BTM tender package (gridforge_power_deploy_spec) with the same comparison rules as gridforge_bids: mandatory non-compliance is never outranked by price, incomplete responses are disqualified not guessed at, and installation method and evidence quality are left to an engineer. Send the same deployment request and architecture the package was built from, plus the completed response schedules.

ride_through_hours.description: the outage duration a battery must be sized against; defaults to 2h if omitted

interconnection.description: utility, pcc_voltage_kV, import_capacity_MW — feeds the interconnection readiness gate. Omitting it leaves that gate MISSING_DATA, never a guessed PASS.

permitting.description: e.g. {emissions_status, noise_status} — feeds the permitting readiness gate.

auth.note: gridforge_qualify and gridforge_estimate are free and need no key. Everything else meters.

payg.billing_rule: A month's charge is the net ledger units for the UTC month (charges minus refunds) at €2 a unit, invoiced monthly in arrears. A month whose charge is under the €5 minimum invoice is not invoiced on its own: it is carried forward and added to the next month, and so on from month to month. A balance that never reaches €5 is never invoiced. A request that is rejected, unauthorised, invalid or fails is refunded and never charged, and a retry with the same Idempotency-Key is never charged twice. Free-allowance usage is never invoiced. The customer's own monthly cap is a hard stop: beyond it the engine answers 402 and nothing more accrues.

evidence_note: Every numeric field in a response carries an evidence class (E0 assumed … E7 observed in operation) and a provenance digest. An agent consuming these must not present an E0 or E1 figure as a property of the physical asset. The calibration block states how far this engine has been reconciled against site data; where it says uncalibrated, it means uncalibrated.
